claim: Analytical and numerical models predict that more homogenous capillary blood flow facilitates oxygen delivery to tissue.
source: Both analytical and numerical models of oxygen advection and diffusion in microvascular networks predict that more homogenous capillary blood flow facilitates oxygen delivery to tissue (Jespersen and Østergaard, 2012; Østergaard et al., 2013; Østergaard et al., 2014a; Østergaard et al., 2014b; Rasmussen et al., 2015).

claim: Capillary blood flow homogeneity during functional activation in the brain has been reported in healthy anesthetized animals.

claim: Capillary flow homogeneity was absent in the mouse model of Alzheimer's disease.

claim: Increased capillary blood flow heterogeneity was found in patients of Alzheimer's disease.
source: while increased capillary blood flow heterogeneity was found in patients of Alzheimer's disease (Eskildsen et al., 2017; Nielsen et al., 2017)
evidence: This is a statement about findings from cited studies.

claim: There is a possible link between disturbed capillary flow patterns, reduced oxygen supply to tissue, and the progression of neurodegeneration.

claim: Lower capillary transit time heterogeneity in cortical layers IV and V than in the upper layers was previously reported in anesthetized mice.

claim: Capillary RBC flow is correlated positively with Mean-PO2.

claim: The temporal resolution of measurements was 0.6 s.
source: The temporal resolution of our measurements (0.6 s) ensured that the blood flow and PO2 fluctuations due to cardiac and respiratory cycles, as they occurred to awake mice, were averaged out

claim: The temporal resolution of 0.6 s is sufficient to capture the dynamics related to the rate of oxygen consumption.
source: but it is sufficient to capture the dynamics related to the rate of oxygen consumption, which could be estimated as the time for tissue PO2 to drop to zero after blood flow stoppage. As reported in cats, that time was at least several seconds (Acker and Lübbers, 1977; Whalen and Nair, 1975).

claim: Blood flow responses to neuronal activation could typically be resolved with 0.6 s temporal resolution.

claim: Positive correlation was observed between the fluctuations of RBC flux and extravascular (tissue) PO2 measured adjacent to capillaries in rat tumor.
source: This observation is in agreement with the previously reported positive correlation between the fluctuations of RBC flux and extravascular (tissue) PO2 measured adjacent to the capillaries in rat tumor, although the latter occurred at a lower frequency range (Braun et al., 1999; Kimura et al., 1996).

claim: Most oxygen in the blood is bound to the hemoglobin inside RBCs.
source: This result could be expected, since most oxygen in the blood is bound to the hemoglobin inside RBCs (Pittman, 2011).

claim: EAT is directly related to the intravascular resistance to the diffusive oxygen transport from RBCs to tissue.
source: Since EAT is directly related to the intravascular resistance to the diffusive oxygen transport from RBCs to tissue (Hellums, 1977), reduced EAT in the deeper layers represents another example of the adaptation of the microvascular network in order to facilitate local oxygen delivery in cortical regions with higher oxygen demand (Pries et al., 1994; Pries et al., 1998; Reglin et al., 2009; Reglin et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement about the relationship between EAT and oxygen transport with citations.

claim: Reduced EAT in deeper layers represents an adaptation of the microvascular network to facilitate local oxygen delivery in cortical regions with higher oxygen demand.
source: Since EAT is directly related to the intravascular resistance to the diffusive oxygen transport from RBCs to tissue (Hellums, 1977), reduced EAT in the deeper layers represents another example of the adaptation of the microvascular network in order to facilitate local oxygen delivery in cortical regions with higher oxygen demand (Pries et al., 1994; Pries et al., 1998; Reglin et al., 2009; Reglin et al., 2017).
evidence: This is presented as an interpretation of findings with supporting citations.

claim: EAT may be affected by multiple parameters, such as RBC spacing, shape and wall-to-RBC spatial clearance.
source: However, it is important to note that mechanisms that govern EAT are multifactorial. EAT may be affected by multiple parameters, such as RBC spacing, shape and wall-to-RBC spatial clearance (Golub and Pittman, 2005; Lücker et al., 2017; Popel, 1989).
evidence: This is a statement about factors affecting EAT with citations.

claim: Capillary transit time is shorter in the surface cortical layers.

evidence: This is presented as a suggestion supported by cited theoretical studies.

claim: Approximately 1/3 of the total oxygen extraction took place along the paths from the pial arterioles to the A1 capillary segments in layers I-III.

claim: Anesthesia suppressed cerebral oxygen metabolism and possibly increased both CBF and arteriolar surface area due to vasodilation.

source: Indeed, it has been recently reported that only ~0.4% of the cortical capillaries in healthy mice had 'stalled flow', but in transgenic mice of Alzheimer's disease the fraction was as high as 2% (Cruz Hernandez et al., 2016; Momjian-Mayor and Baron, 2005).

claim: In transgenic mice of Alzheimer's disease, approximately 2% of cortical capillaries had 'stalled flow'.
source: Indeed, it has been recently reported that only ~0.4% of the cortical capillaries in healthy mice had 'stalled flow', but in transgenic mice of Alzheimer's disease the fraction was as high as 2% (Cruz Hernandez et al., 2016; Momjian-Mayor and Baron, 2005).
evidence: This is a statement about findings from cited studies.

claim: A capillary segment with PO2 of approximately 15 mmHg and no detectable RBC flow during the 9-s-long acquisition was identified.

claim: Layer V in mouse barrel cortex spans the depth range of 450–700 μm.

claim: The range of 450–600 μm interrogated in this study likely overlaps the best with the upper part of layer V (i.e., layer Va).

evidence: This is a statement about the probe's properties with citation.

claim: The oxygen saturation of hemoglobin (SO2) was computed based on PO2 using the Hill equation with parameters h = 2.59 and P50 = 40.2 mmHg specific for C57BL/6 mice.

claim: SO2 in capillaries was calculated based on the RBC-PO2.

claim: DOEF in layer I represents the global OEF in the interrogated cortical tissue territory.
